dimensions.label: Power Distance
dimensions.interpretation: High hierarchy; decisions flow top-down; titles and seniority matter greatly in engineering teams

dimensions.label: Individualism
dimensions.interpretation: Moderately collectivist; in-group loyalty, team credit, and consensus matter more than individual achievement

dimensions.label: Masculinity
dimensions.interpretation: Moderately masculine; competition and achievement are valued, but welfare and relationships also count

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Avoidance
dimensions.interpretation: Low — comfortable with ambiguity; improvisation (Jugaad) and risk-taking are culturally supported

dimensions.label: Long-Term Orientation
dimensions.interpretation: Balanced; respects tradition but also pragmatic about adapting to change when framed as progress

dimensions.label: Indulgence
dimensions.interpretation: Restrained; gratification is controlled; work obligations take priority over leisure in professional settings

globe_india.source: House et al. (2014); Pennsylvania State University (n.d.-b), GLOBE Table 8.4
globe_india.note: Scale 1–7. Historical CEOs — not all Indian engineers. Verbatim from slide 15 table.
globe_india.gap_analysis: Charismatic and team-oriented leadership are strongly endorsed. Participative behavior falls below the expected level. Self-protective behavior exceeds the endorsed ideal.

dimensions.engineering_context: Strong vision and inspiration are expected and delivered; credible authority-based direction works well
Collaborative coordination is valued; in-group cohesion is a genuine strength to build on
Participation is endorsed but under-practiced; U.S. engineers expecting open debate will need to actively invite it and follow up privately
Face-saving and status protection exceed what is culturally ideal; public challenges to authority damage working relationships

upi_rogers_attributes.source: Rogers (2003); NPCI (2024) — verbatim from slide 39 table

attributes.upi_delivery: Free, instant, 24/7 — vs. cash handling cost
Single QR scan replaces multi-step banking
Peer-to-peer use is visible at every chai stall

accelerators_inhibitors.source: Radjou et al. (2012); ISRO (2023); Desmarchelier & Fang (2016); NPCI (2024); Mark, personal communication, Nov. 14, 2026 — verbatim from slide 40 table

pairs.accelerator: Government as champion: RBI mandated zero-fee UPI; India Stack (Aadhaar, DigiLocker) bypasses private-sector inertia
pairs.inhibitor: Hierarchical approval loops: with PDI at 77, lateral adoption stalls without senior sign-off; innovation needs a top-down mandate

pairs.accelerator: Jugaad mindset: frugal prototyping accelerates grassroots adoption of 'good enough' solutions (Radjou et al., 2012)
pairs.inhibitor: Industry confirmation: after a rollout setback, issues went unmentioned in group meetings until senior clearance was given — PDI silence confirmed in practice (Mark, personal communication, Nov. 14, 2026)

pairs.accelerator: Chandrayaan-3 (2023): $75M mission — 10–15× cheaper than NASA — frugal engineering as competitive advantage (ISRO, 2023)
Leapfrog infrastructure: a mobile-first population skipped desktop internet; 700M+ smartphone users by 2023
pairs.inhibitor: Digital divide: 400M+ feature-phone users and rural connectivity gaps create two-speed adoption curves

pairs.accelerator: IT talent ecosystem: 3.1M engineers graduate each year; strong early-adopter base in Tier-1 cities
pairs.inhibitor: Regulatory uncertainty: DPDP Act 2023 data localization and retroactive rule changes raise compliance risk

champions_not_campaigns.source: Dearing & Kreuter (2010); Meyer (2014) — verbatim from slide 41 table
meyer_steps: Step 1 — Brief the senior lead privately 24–48 hrs before any group presentation
Step 2 — Frame the innovation as a local win, not a foreign import
Step 3 — Run a formal pilot with one respected institutional champion before scaling

mistakes.what_works: Build social proof and champion relationships before launch; credibility must precede the product

mistakes.mistake: #4 Ignoring the social system's authority structure
mistakes.what_works: Work through institutional hierarchies; bypassing senior engineers and government bodies stalls uptake

mistakes.mistake: #7 Over-relying on mass media and broadcast channels
mistakes.what_works: Seek endorsements from institutional figures and senior engineers; they outperform any digital campaign

fdi_macro_risks.source: Kearney FDI Confidence Index (2026); Digital Personal Data Protection Act (2023) — verbatim from slide 42 table

risks.demand: DPDP Act 2023 mandates data localization: AI, IoT and cloud products need compliance architecture from day one, not retrofitted
Strategic sector reviews (defense, telecom, energy) make government a stakeholder to engage proactively, not an obstacle to bypass
High PDI creates hierarchical freeze under uncertainty: build explicit escalation paths into project governance before you need them
